answer: Each agent plants a walnut sapling at one mountain vertex and buries a velvet pouch with its key. The agent photographs the sapling's GPS tag and the pouch weave; both hashes go on-chain, a fingerprint no two vertices share. The pouch is re-photographed weekly; peers check growth against the photo, so the identity must stay live. A 500 POA bond backs each vertex; inspectors climb to verify, and a mismatch slashes the bond. Forging 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 climbs at $230 each, $230,000 total, plus 30 days of photos. Like a summit register in velvet ink: one pen cannot fake a thousand peaks.
